newsitem.title: GERMANY: Porsche says expects higher 1996/97 sales, profit.
newsitem.headline: Porsche says expects higher 1996/97 sales, profit.

text.p: German sportscar maker Porsche AG said on Friday that it expected to report higher full-year 1996/1997 sales and profit after first-half profit more than trebled.
Porsche chairman Weldelin Wiedeking told the group's annual general meeting the group's recovery has taken hold.
"What has happened so far leads us to assume sales and profit will climb further for the year," Wiedeking said in a text of a speech prepared for the meeting.
Porsche earlier on Friday said sales for the first half of its business year which ends July 31 rose to 1.7 billion marks from 1.42 billion marks in the year-ago period.
Provisional net profit surged to 36 million marks from 10 million marks in the first six months as vehicle deliveries rose to 12,800 units from 10,208 units in the 1995/1996 period.
In the 1995/96 business year, Porsche reported sales of 2.81 billion marks and net profit of 48.1 billion marks.
